title: Sale / Savings Substantiation — F5-SALE-HAS-DATES
quote: 'sale' language with no start/end date (perpetual-sale risk).
recommendation: Add genuine start/end dates to sale/savings claims; perpetual sales imply no real prior price.

title: CARS Act Total-Payable Disclosure — CA-CARS-003
quote: Monthly payment advertised on vdp without the total amount payable over the term.
statute: Cal. Civ. Code §1784.41(c)(1) (CARS Act, SB 766) | CALIFORNIA controls: CARS Act (SB 766, Cal. Civ. Code §1784.20 et seq.), operative Oct 1, 2026. The federal FTC CARS Rule (16 CFR Part 463) was VACATED by the 5th Circuit (Jan 2025) and formally WITHDRAWN from the CFR (Fed. Reg. Feb 2026) — not enforceable. Subsection pin-cites verified against the chaptered statute (leginfo) 2026-06-28.
recommendation: California's CARS-style requirement is not operative until Oct 1, 2026 — fix now to be ready. This is a CALIFORNIA requirement, not a federal one. Under the CARS Act (operative Oct 1, 2026) any monthly-payment ad must also disclose the total the consumer will have paid after all scheduled payments.

Please visually double-check this item. Add descriptive alt text to images. Missing alt text is the most commonly cited issue in serial ADA/Unruh dealer-website suits.

title: Accessibility (ADA/Unruh) — ADA-FORM-LABELS

statute: ADA Title III; Cal. Civ. Code §51 (Unruh); WCAG 2.1 1.3.1/4.1.2

Please visually double-check this item. Give every input a programmatic label (<label for>, aria-label, or aria-labelledby). Unlabeled lead-form fields are a frequent ADA/Unruh claim.

quote: Homepage structure gaps: no skip-to-content link (WCAG 2.4.1).

title: Lease headline payment/DAS does not match its own disclosure (X7 xDrive40i)
quote: X7 xDRIVE40i VIN 5UX23EM00V9563400 card headline: $983/mo, $9,962 due at signing. Same-VIN disclosure modal: 'at $1,049 for 39 months ... $7,398 due at signing.'
statute: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17500; Cal. Veh. Code §11713.16
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — The on-card headline figure is a rendered visual element the crawler read, not raw disclosure text, so the exact card values must be confirmed on the live page. If confirmed, the advertised monthly payment ($983) and due-at-signing ($9,962) directly contradict the vehicle's own OFFER DETAILS disclosure ($1,049/mo, $7,398 DAS); a reasonable consumer would be misled about true cost. Reconcile the card and modal to a single accurate figure.

title: Two conflicting lease disclosures for the same VIN (X3 30 xDrive)
quote: X3 30 xDRIVE VIN 5UX53GP09T9560836 appears twice: one disclosure 'Selling price $51,790 ... $0.25/mile over 10,000 miles/year ... $5,007 due at signing'; a second 'Selling price $52,050.00 ... over 7500 miles/year ... $5,300.86 due at signing.'
statute: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17500; Cal. Veh. Code §11713.16
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — Two OFFER DETAILS modals for the identical VIN carry different selling price ($51,790 vs $52,050), different due-at-signing, and different mileage allowance (10,000 vs 7,500 mi/yr). Confirm on the live page whether both render, then remove the stale/duplicate offer so a single, internally consistent set of lease terms is shown for the vehicle.

title: Two different selling prices shown for the same new vehicle (lease vs finance tab)
quote: Lease disclosure: 'Selling price $61,015.00.' Finance disclosure (same VIN 3MW69CW04T8G27347): 'Selling price $62,515.00.'
statute: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17500; Cal. Veh. Code §11713.1
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — The lease-tab and finance-tab present two different 'Selling price' figures ($61,015 vs $62,515, a $1,500 gap not attributable to the $85 doc fee) for the same VIN. A lease cap-cost reduction can explain a lower lease price, but showing two figures both labeled 'Selling price' invites consumer confusion about the actual vehicle price. Label each figure with the offer it belongs to (e.g., lease cap cost vs cash/finance price) or reconcile to one selling price. Pattern recurs on new VDPs site-wide.

title: Used vehicle price labeled 'MSRP' in finance disclosure; on-card price differs by $85
quote: Finance this 2024 BMW X3 sDRIVE30i ... MSRP $28,585.00. Selling price $28,585.00 ... [on-card Selling Price shown as $28,670]
statute: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17500; Cal. Veh. Code §11713.1
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — The Reg Z finance disclosure labels a used (64,172-mile) 2024 X3's price as 'MSRP $28,585.00'; a used vehicle has no manufacturer's suggested retail price, so this label is inaccurate. Separately, the on-card 'Selling Price' ($28,670, which includes the $85 doc fee) differs by $85 from the finance/CarStory figure ($28,585), showing two price figures for one VIN. Relabel the used-car figure (e.g., 'Price' or 'Selling Price'), and reconcile the doc-fee treatment so a single selling price is presented.

title: 'Dealer Discount' taken off the dealer's own List Price (reference-price substantiation)
quote: List Price $32,995, Dealer Discount -$4,410, Doc Fee +$85, Selling Price $28,670.
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — The advertised savings ('Dealer Discount -$4,410') is measured against the dealer's own 'List Price,' not a manufacturer or bona fide prior price, which B&P §17501 scrutinizes as a savings reference. Mitigating factor already present: an independent CarStory market report ('$3,623 below predicted market average ... GREAT DEAL') is shown alongside, which substantiates the value claim. Confirm the List Price reflects a genuine prior/asking price or reframe the comparison around the independent CarStory benchmark. Recurring pattern on used/CPO VDPs.

title: CPO/used vehicle price labeled 'MSRP' in finance disclosure; on-card price differs by $85
quote: Finance this 2023 BMW i4 eDrive35 Gran Coupe ... MSRP $30,085.00. Selling price $30,085.00 ... [on-card Selling Price shown as $30,170]
statute: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §17500; Cal. Veh. Code §11713.1
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — The finance disclosure labels a used/CPO (33,734-mile) i4's price as 'MSRP $30,085.00'; a pre-owned vehicle has no manufacturer's suggested retail price. The on-card 'Selling Price' ($30,170, incl. $85 doc fee) also differs by $85 from the finance/CarStory figure. Relabel the used figure and reconcile the doc-fee treatment to one selling price.

title: Blanket 'includes all offers and incentives' without identifying which incentives apply
quote: New vehicle pricing includes all offers and incentives. Tax, Title and Tags not included in vehicle prices shown ...
recommendation: Advertised pricing states it 'includes all offers and incentives' but does not identify which specific incentives are baked in or their eligibility conditions (loyalty, conquest, military, college grad, finance-through-lender, etc.). A consumer who does not qualify for a stacked incentive may not be able to obtain the shown price. List the incentives included and their qualification criteria, or add 'not all buyers will qualify' with a link to terms. Same disclaimer recurs on the used and CPO listing pages.

title: Monthly-payment estimate basis assumes a 20% down payment
quote: **With approved credit. Terms may vary. Monthly payments are only estimates derived from the vehicle price with a 72 month term, 4.9% interest and 20% downpayment.
recommendation: The payment-estimate basis (72 mo / 4.9% / 20% down) is disclosed, which is good practice, but a 20% down assumption is aggressive relative to typical financing and lowers the displayed estimate. Ensure the assumption is presented near the estimate on the VDP (not only in the footer) so consumers understand the payment shown presumes a substantial down payment.

title: Lease payment used as the headline element on specials cards and VDPs
quote: Each card headline: 'Lease for $X Per month for Y Months, Plus tax and license. $Z Due At Signing' — lease payment shown in large type as the headline; MSRP not shown on cards (only inside the disclosure).
statute: BMW Brand Guidelines for Retail (March 2026) — Pricing: MSRP Presentation
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — Prominence/layout claim that cannot be fully verified from text. BMW-PRICE-001 states pricing (lease, APR, credits, MSRP) may not appear in headlines except for FMAs, banner ads, paid search, and paid social. On these organic dealer-site special cards (and the VDP hero), the lease monthly payment is the dominant headline element. Confirm the rendered visual hierarchy; if the payment is the headline, restructure so the model/offer name is the headline and the payment sits in a supporting position to align with BMW retail guidelines and co-op eligibility.

The vehicle is served on a /cpo/ (Certified) URL but the page reads like a standard used listing with no BMW Certified branding and no certification warranty/coverage terms. Verify on the live page. If it is genuinely BMW Certified, add the correct 'BMW Certified' logo and coverage/warranty terms; if it is not certified, move it off the /cpo/ path so certification is not implied.

title: 'Car' used instead of BMW-preferred 'vehicle' across the site

statute: BMW Brand Guidelines for Retail (March 2026) — Ad Copy: Vehicle vs Car Terminology
recommendation: BMW-COPY-002 directs use of 'vehicle' rather than 'car' in BMW communications. Listing-page headings, the finance-department copy, and VDP URL slugs use 'car(s)'. Where dealer-controlled (headings, body copy), prefer 'vehicle'. Advisory only; SEO-driven page titles may warrant an exception, so apply judgment.

title: Third-party lender/financing module interleaved with BMW pricing content

A 'Real-Time Lenders' financing widget interleaved with BMW Financial Services lease/finance figures could blur BMW vs third-party financing. title: Headlines rendered in Title Case rather than BMW UPPER CASE convention
quote: Page title/headline: 'Your Go-To BMW Dealer in Alhambra, CA'.
statute: BMW Brand Guidelines for Retail (March 2026) — Typography: Headline and Body Copy Case Rules

BMW-TYPO-002 specifies headlines/subheads in UPPER CASE (Title Case reserved for CTA buttons). Confirm which on-page elements are true headlines vs SEO title tags, then apply BMW case rules to dealer-controlled headline copy. Low-risk best-practice item.

title: Used vehicle pages do not reference the CARS Act 3-day cancellation right
quote: Used Cars for Sale ... Cards list VIN, Stock #, ... 'Disclosure', 'Check Availability' ... [no reference to a 3-day cancellation right]
recommendation: **NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW AND VERIFICATION** — Absence-based, best-practice observation. Under SB 766 (operative Oct 1, 2026), used vehicles $50,000 or less carry a 3-day cancellation right; the primary disclosure is at point of sale, so website silence is not itself a violation. No contradictory 'all sales final' or waiver language was found (the ComplyAuto arbitration/class-action waiver applies to privacy disputes, not vehicle-purchase cancellation). Ahead of the operative date, consider adding an accurate reference to the 3-day right (3 calendar days, $50K threshold, statutory restocking-fee limits) on used VDPs/VLPs.
